LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns, part of Strand 11 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: when, where, whose, who and what) sentences, 1. Why do we ask questions? 2. Which words do we use to ask questions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. realise the importance of interrogatives in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner uses appropriate interrogatives to ask questions.

• Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with digital devices to watch videos and type sentences.

Values:
• Unity: The learner collaborates with peers to perform task such as watching videos and typing sentences on a digital

device.

• Respect: This is promoted as the learner is able to accommodate the views of others during the discussion.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-esteem: This is built in the learner as they ask and answer questions using interrogatives about their favourite sports

making them discover their talents.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of interrogatives to question and answer sessions in Religious Education among other

learning areas.
